title: UNI2 layered scene: CG + .pat part set 991 (additive flame, PRAS pivots, 3D ring arcs)
notes: Additive point-sampled and PRFL-filtered .pat parts over the CG layer; the stage Bokashi pass and aura glow are modelled for every tool alike.
caveat: Known residual for ours: the ring arcs (set 991 slots 41/44/45) change between game runs (render-match17); the per-layer bokashi split (--layers) is off here because only our editor can export per-layer shots.

title: UNI2 rotated CG mid-tween (AFHK 1 interpolation, AFAZ rotation lerp, tick 27 of 55)
notes: Needs AFHK interpolation between two keyframes plus a rotated, palette-indexed CG sprite.
caveat: gonp has no animation playback, so it is shown at frame 0 (the keyframe tick 27 belongs to); its failure here is the sprite decode/palette, not only the missing tween.

title: UNI2 PUPS palette switch: CG 869 + .pat set 839 with PPPA-tinted parts
pattern_frame: chr027 p449 f4 (zoom 1.5 editor vs zoom 1 game)
notes: Palette bank chosen by the pattern's PUPS, plus per-part palette (PPPA) tint on the .pat layer.
caveat: Close-up: v2_model drops view-wide rows/columns from every footprint (its grid-line guard), so only the lower-right of the sprite is scored, the same pixels for every tool.

title: UNI2 .pat-only pattern with PRRV 3 (H+V flipped) streak parts
notes: Pure .pat effect (no CG sprite on the frame): a tool without .pat support draws nothing.

title: MBTL p238: translucent tray (.pat set 275, PRAL 1 + translucent parts) at real zoom 1.5
MBTL p157: additive arcs (PRRV 2) + the puddle effect at real zoom 1.5
caveat: The puddle (p158 spawn) is in the game frame; scored pixels are the union of the tools' footprints, so game-only pixels outside every tool's footprint are not scored.

title: MBTL CG sprite at zoom 1.5 with the game's CG zoom filter (Filter_V) and BgColor light
notes: Plain idle sprite: every tool loads it; the difference is the zoom filter. The training frame counter box is excluded.
caveat: Control-style case (one CG sprite) to show the zoom filter, not a complex scene. sosfiro and gonp give identical numbers: neither applies the game's CG zoom filter (Filter_V) at 1.5x.
